Black-tailed water vole ( Rissa tridactyla ).
Dorsal colour is black and the venter is darker with the centre and base darker than the venter. There is a median black stripe down the back of the animal. Individuals with white tails are rare so tail colour is an unreliable guide to sex and may differ in colour year to year. The species has a wide range comprising large parts of southern England and neighbouring parts of Wales and eastern Scotland.
